obligations.summary: A notified body must be established under the national law of a Member State and must have legal personality.
Notified bodies must satisfy organisational, quality management, resources, process, and cybersecurity requirements necessary to fulfil their tasks.

Notified bodies must maintain an organisational structure, allocation of responsibilities, reporting lines, and operations that ensure confidence in their performance and in the results of conformity assessment activities.

Notified bodies must be independent of the provider of any high-risk AI system for which they perform conformity assessment, as well as of any other operator with an economic interest in assessed systems and any competitors of the provider.
exceptions: Use of assessed high-risk AI systems necessary for the operations of the conformity assessment body is permitted
Use of such high-risk AI systems for personal purposes is permitted

obligations.summary: Notified bodies, their top-level management, and conformity assessment personnel must not be directly involved in the design, development, marketing, or use of high-risk AI systems, must not represent parties engaged in those activities, and must not engage in any activity conflicting with their independence or integrity, including consultancy services.

Notified bodies must be organised and operated to safeguard independence, objectivity, and impartiality, and must document and implement structures and procedures promoting impartiality throughout their organisation, personnel, and assessment activities.

Notified bodies must have documented procedures ensuring that all personnel, committees, subsidiaries, subcontractors, and associated bodies maintain confidentiality of information obtained during conformity assessment activities in accordance with Article 78, and staff must observe professional secrecy except in relation to national notifying authorities.
exceptions: Disclosure is permitted when required by law
Disclosure to the notifying authorities of the Member State in which activities are carried out is permitted

obligations.summary: Notified bodies must have procedures for performing conformity assessment activities that take due account of the size of the provider, the sector in which it operates, its structure, and the complexity of the AI system concerned.
Notified bodies must take out appropriate liability insurance for their conformity assessment activities.
exceptions: Liability insurance is not required if liability is assumed by the Member State in accordance with national law
Liability insurance is not required if the Member State is itself directly responsible for the conformity assessment

obligations.summary: Notified bodies must be capable of carrying out all their tasks under this Regulation with the highest degree of professional integrity and requisite competence in the specific field, whether performed by themselves or on their behalf.

Notified bodies must have sufficient internal competences to effectively evaluate tasks conducted by external parties on their behalf, and must maintain permanent availability of sufficient administrative, technical, legal, and scientific personnel with relevant expertise in AI systems, data, data computing, and applicable requirements.

Notified bodies must participate in coordination activities as referred to in Article 38 and must take part in, or be represented in, European standardisation organisations, or otherwise ensure they remain aware of and up to date with relevant standards.
